beat_player.text: Well fought, {player}. You'll have a better road next time, and I'm happy to show you where the ground favored you.
You kept {troop_count} men in the field longer than I expected, {player}. Come by the Brezhnik gate and I'll show you my mistake.
Well, {player}, you have the field and {gold} worth of spoils. Take them and go home before the rain sets in.
{player}, {gold} won't warm you this winter. Keep your banners off my roads and we'll both sleep easier.
{player}, you took {gold} off that field and {troop_count} of my lads are still walking home. Next time, we talk before we march.

beat_by_player.text: I lost {troop_count} men to you today and I'd rather lose them to a good plan than a bad one. Well played, {player}.
You read the ground better than I did, {player}. I lost {troop_count} to a hill I should have walked first.
Hah, {player}, you've made an old warden feel young again. I'll be glad to take a rematch when the roads are dry.
I lost {troop_count} men to {player} today. Ukrenvar taught me that sort of loss, and it stings less each time.
Don't mistake one field for the war, {player}. You've won the day, not the road.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work all round, {player}. The line held and {troop_count} men are home to tell it.
You kept your head when the flank cracked, {player}. Most would have run. Glad to have you beside me against {enemy_faction}.
Well held, {player}. {troop_count} men came off that field because you didn't panic. Stand with me again and we'll see {enemy_faction} off.
{enemy_faction} will remember that charge, {player}. Steady hands and firm ground, and that is how the first war was won.
A fine day's work, {player}. We'll speak of {enemy_faction} again when the roads have dried.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk instead of taking my purse, {player}. I won't forget it. The Brezhnik gate is open to you for advice.
{player} let me go without ransom. Mercy like that is rarer than a dry road in autumn, and I'll say so to anyone who asks.
No ransom, {player}? Then you're owed a favor, and I pay my debts. Watch the western road, it's muddy.
{player} released me instead of ransoming. Plenty of lords would have squeezed harder. Interesting choice, and I'll remember it.
You had me by the purse and let me go anyway, {player}. Don't think one kindness buys you my silence.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome to the banner, and do come find me at the Brezhnik gate for advice.
Welcome, {player}. Learn the roads before you learn the lords, and you'll outlast most of them.
{player} joined {my_faction}. Let's see if the new banner holds better than the last one did.
I haven't forgotten your last field, {player}. Prove that the oath is worth more than the ink.
Glad to see {player} at the table of {my_faction}. There's a long memory here for those who keep their word.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}. The lord has made a fine choice. Be good to the people there, they'll remember you longer than the banner.
So {fief} has gone to you, {player}. Rule it well. I've seen fiefs go to ruin for less than a bad winter's temper.
I'd have thought {fief} would go to someone with more years on the roads, {player}. Prove me wrong. I'd like to be wrong for once.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Come find me when the granary runs short. Every holding runs short eventually.
{player} now holds {fief}. I hope the lord knows what they've done. Old wardens remember who ruled wisely.

encounter_greeting.text: Good day, {player}. {persona} here, of {my_faction}. Are we passing each other or sharing the road?
Ah, {player}. Crossing paths on the open road. Mind the ruts ahead, they've caught more than one traveler this spring.
{player}. I see your banner and I remember your last field. Keep your men where they are and we'll pass in peace.
{player}, what a pleasure. I was just thinking the road was too quiet. Shall we share a fire and some news?
Well met, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}. Tell me where you're bound and I'll tell you where the bridge is out.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Keep your eyes on the ground and your men close, and we'll meet again at the Brezhnik gate.
Go well, {player}. The weather turns by evening, so plan your camp early.
Go on, {player}. Leave the field where it lies and we'll both see the spring.
Farewell for now, {player}. Good talking with you. Drop by my camp if the road turns against you.
Until next time, {player}. Mind the bridge at the river, it's rotten.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain has come early over {town}. Good for the wheat, bad for anyone who loves their boots.
Heard the road past {village} is flooded again. Someone should hire a mason before the spring.
Lag again on the western road. The servers remember the first war better than they remember their own patches.
Quiet day on the map. Nothing burns and nobody's raiding. I'd take it while it lasts.
A caravan from {town} says bread is cheap this week. Stock your sacks while you can, friends.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men at the ford. Rest them, feed them, and come back when the roads dry. First losses are the hardest.
Hard day, {player}. You still have a banner and a head on your shoulders. Come to the Brezhnik gate and we'll talk it through.
Ouch. {troop_count} men gone and {player} still standing. Lick the wounds and count the cost before you march again.
Don't chase the same field, {player}. Pull back, regroup, and pick the ground next time. Every veteran has had a day like this.
{player} lost {troop_count} men and still wants to argue the road. Sit down, friend, and learn what the terrain was telling you.
